messages:
support_jen: Customer OrbitPay hit a sudden quality drop + billing spike after a regional failover. They reported truncated responses and weird tokenization. Request id: req_0a3f9b; intended region: us-east-1 but headers show eu-west-1 and model 'redwood-quant-lite-v1'. Can oncall take a look?

infra_alex: Looking now — can you paste the raw curl + response headers and a short example of the truncated output? Any auth errors or 5xx?

support_jen: Pasted sample below. No 5xx, auth ok.
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_0a3f9b" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-compat-v2","input":"Invoice #1234 — total: $5,000. Please list line items."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-served-region: eu-west-1
x-served-model: redwood-quant-lite-v1
x-token-count: 412
content-type: application/json

{"id":"resp_9c3","output":"Line items:\n1. Subscription - Basic Plan — $49\n2. Extra seat x5 — $250\n3. Taxes — $..."}  <-- truncated mid-value, no function-calling JSON
```

eng_runtime_maya: That header is the smoking gun — the request was routed to the lite quantized variant. redwood-quant-lite-v1 uses a different tokenization path and smaller capability set; it will frequently drop structured/function outputs and can truncate earlier. Failover policy should prefer tokenizer-compatible variants.

oncall_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-441. Assigned to eng-runtime. Labels: region-failover, model-variant, billing-impact.

infra_alex: Router logs show us-east pool flapped at 2480012301 and we routed to standby in eu-west. The standby mapping was 'standby-default' which currently maps to quant-lite. So two issues: cross-region routing + incompatible standby mapping. Attaching router snippet (sanitized):
```
[router] decision=req_0a3f9b region_pref=us-east -> fallback_region=eu-west pool=standby-default served_model=redwood-quant-lite-v1
```

ml_eva: Lite quantization changed token boundaries (byte-level merges), which increases token counts and sometimes breaks punctuation/json boundaries. Example: input containing em-dash or currency formatting often re-tokenizes into extra tokens and can break function-calling outputs, so truncation + billing spike is expected.

support_jen: Customer says billing for that hour jumped ~3x compared to baseline. They lost invoice parsing output (function call). They want the session backfilled and a credit.

billing_nate: We'll need all request IDs + token counts (client header + x-token-count) to adjudicate. If this was a platform failover that changed tokenizer family, we can offer pro-rated credit. Also recommending we add a guard: if served_model.tokenizer_family != requested_model.tokenizer_family then don't apply 'standard' billing (or mark for review).

eng_runtime_maya: Preparing a hotfix: update router standby mapping to prefer same-tokenizer-family variants (compat table) and block lite variants for customers using function-calling or pinned compat models. I'll roll a config update to us-east fallback rules now (2m ETA). Also adding metric failover_variant_compat to alert on high rates.

infra_alex: Rolled the config update to us-east. I also pinned OrbitPay tenant to redwood-compat-v2 in the routing table as a temporary mitigation. Can support ask them to retry the same request id?

support_jen: Told OrbitPay: we pinned you to redwood-compat-v2, please re-run your test with same input and send new headers. Offered temporary credit pending billing review. Will follow up when they confirm. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ml_eva: Follow-up: we'll run a short audit across failover mappings to ensure no other tenants are routed to tokenization-incompatible standbys. I'll kick off a sweep job and share results.

billing_nate: Once we have the list of affected request ids, I'll prepare credit estimates and send to CS for approval.

support_jen: Closing loop here when OrbitPay confirms. Keeping thread open for the audit results.
